name: Dreierles (Baden Tarock)
description: Dreierles (also known as Dreierle or Dreier) is a sophisticated trick-taking game from the Baden region of Germany, played with a 54-card Cego (Tarot) deck. It belongs to the Tarock family and is closely related to Austrian Tapp Tarock. In Dreierles, a single declarer plays against a team of opponents, utilizing a six-card 'blind' (talon) from which they draw exactly three cards to improve their hand, giving the game its name.

It belongs to the Tarock family and is closely related to Austrian Tapp Tarock. In Dreierles, a single declarer plays against a team of opponents, utilizing a six-card 'blind' (talon) from which they draw exactly three cards to improve their hand, giving the game its name.

history.origins: Dreierles survived as a niche tradition in central Baden (around Rastatt) alongside the better known Cego. It likely shares an ancestor with 19th-century Austrian Tarock variants, possibly imported during the era of the Austrian garrisons in the Rastatt federal fortress.
timeline: 1820s: Early forms of Tapp Tarock emerge in Central Europe.
1850s: Tarock games become established in the Baden military and social clubs.
Modern Era: Maintained by dedicated groups in Steinmauern and the Achertal region.
history.cultural: Played in traditional 'GasthÃ¶fe' (inns) and family circles; it is one of the few surviving German card games to use a full 54ndcard Tarot deck.
history.evolution: While Cego became the 'national game' of Baden, Dreierles preserved a more traditional Tarock structure with fewer contracts and a fixed three-card draw mechanic.

setup.players: Usually 3 players. If 4 play, the dealer sits out the hand.
setup.deck: 54-card Cego pack. Consists of 22 Tarocks (Trumps), 16 Court cards (K, Q, C, J), and 16 pip cards (Leere).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 16 cards (in batches of 4). 6 cards are dealt face-down to the center to form the 'Blind' (Talon).

rules.objective: Score more than 35 points (out of 70 total) for the declarer, or prevent the declarer from doing so for the defenders.
rules.gameplay:
1. Bidding: Players bid for the right to be the declarer. The highest bid wins.
2. The Draw: The declarer takes any 3 cards from the 6-card blind and discards 3 non-scoring cards (Leere) in their place.
3. Trick Play: Standard Tarock rules. Trumps (Tarocks) always win against suit cards. You MUST follow suit or play a trump if void.
keyRules: Red suits (Hearts/Diamonds) rank: King (High), Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 1, 2, 3, 4 (Low).
Black suits (Spades/Clubs) rank: King (High), Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7 (Low).
The GstieÃŸ (Fool) is the highest trump.
Pfeife (trump 1) bonus: if the declarer wins the last trick with the Pfeife, they receive extra game points from each opponent; if it loses, they pay.

strategy.basic: As declarer, use the 3ndcard draw to complete your trump sequences or to 'void' a suit so you can trump in later.
strategy.intermediate: Teamwork: Defenders must work together to 'bleed' the declarer's trumps using their long suits.
strategy.advanced: The Pagat Ultimo: Keeping the Tarock 1 until the very last trick requires impeccable card counting and timing, as it is easily lost if trumps are led early.
